metadata.case_name: WONG YUEN MEI v. YOUNG YAU YAU CECELIA

source: The Defendant prescribed a course of orthodontic treatment (“the treatment”) which involved the extraction of her 4 first molars with regular check-up sessions about once every 2 weeks after the extraction.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

injuries.description: tooth decay in 13 of her teeth
source: Food would be trapped in those gaps, which resulted in tooth decay in 13 of her teeth.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of hard dental tissues and pulp

injuries.description: the 2nd molars of the Plaintiff were tipped and tilted
source: Dr. Ling found that the 2nd molars of the Plaintiff were tipped and tilted, the grinding surfaces of the teeth would be adversely affected and the ordinary chewing function would diminish.

injuries.description: mild temporo-mandibular joint dysfunctions (symptoms of pain and of the clicking and crepitus of jaw joints)
source: Further, the Plaintiff is found to have symptoms of mild temporo-mandibular joint dysfunctions, which included the symptoms of pain and of the clicking and crepitus of jaw joints.

manifestations.description: her upper teeth could not fit comfortably with her lower teeth
she suffered from ulcer of gum, causing serious pain when she ate, drank or spoke
she also suffered from headache, depression, anxiety and insomnia
due to the above problems, she could not discharge her duties properly as a flight attendant, including but not limited to the making of announcements to passengers
she could not chew food properly. By reason thereof, she have to cut food into small pieces and swallow the food without chewing
that caused her to suffer from serious loss of appetite and serious loss of weight
Food would be trapped in those gaps
symptoms of pain and of the clicking and crepitus of jaw joints

treatments_received: regular orthodontic check-up sessions about once every 2 weeks after the extraction
remedial treatment from Dr. Leung Ting On
treatment by Dr. Yu Kin Kuen for tooth decay
consultation/advice from Dr. Lee Man Biu
examination by Dr. John K.Y. Ling

Special damages items incurred (Defendant’s dental fees and disbursements $26,480; Dr. Lee’s dental fees and disbursements $1,000; Dr. Leung’s dental fees and disbursements $31,540; Dr. Yu’s dental fees and disbursements $3,330; 30 packs of special teeth floss $1,395; 30 packs of special mini-brushes $1,497; transportation expenses $1,000; Total: $66,242)
treatments_future: further remedial treatment sessions with Dr. Leung Ting On ($750x2) $1,500

losses.description: Due to the extraction of her 4 first molars, there are now huge gaps between her teeth, which cannot close up significantly despite Dr. Leung’s effort. Food would be trapped in those gaps, which resulted in tooth decay in 13 of her teeth.
the Plaintiff feels upset and depressed. She also feels uncomfortable with her appearance.

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy food and drink
losses.description: she could not chew food properly. By reason thereof, she have to cut food into small pieces and swallow the food without chewing; that caused her to suffer from serious loss of appetite and serious loss of weight.
due to the above problems, she could not discharge her duties properly as a flight attendant, including but not limited to the making of announcements to passengers
she also suffered from headache, depression, anxiety and insomnia

comparable_cases.case_name: Lee Hau Chi Mariam Teresa v. Chung Chee Keung Peter & ors.
comparable_cases.injury_description: the Plaintiff received a prolonged and underperformed orthodontic treatment by having her 4 first premolars extracted. She has suffered unnecessary pain and sufferings in having to undergo a 2nd surgery.
